entries.title: 20 · Exact complex amplitudes: basis changes, interference and round-trip checks
entries.summary: A CG matrix can contain real radicals while the state has imaginary components. Exact expressions help verify phases, norms, and inverse transformations.

entries.title: 21 · Triple  tensor product : from  coupling path  to a Racah matrix
entries.summary: Fix the final representation first, then label every path by its intermediate representation and two outer multiplicities. Recoupling connects two bases of the same subspace.

entries.title: 22 · Exact Racah and 6j coefficients: radicals from three 3 representations
entries.summary: Compute overlaps directly in the highest-weight subspace spanned by three product states, then distinguish the unitary Racah matrix from dimension-scaled 6j coefficients.

entries.title: 23 · Complex phases and two-body operators in  recoupling
entries.summary: Track path-amplitude phases exactly, and move a two-factor interaction that is diagonal in one coupling basis into another.

entries.title: 24 · Fourfold  tensor product : pairing trees, crossings, and three levels of path labels
entries.summary: Expand the (AB)(CD) and (AC)(BD) paths in the same A,B,C,D order and compare the copy spaces of the final representation.

entries.title: 25 · Exact 9j coefficients: a 3×3 matrix from four product states
entries.summary: Construct exact paths from highest-weight conditions and pair-exchange symmetries, then distinguish unitary recoupling R from the dimension-reduced 9j table S.

entries.title: 26 · Physical uses of four-body recoupling: color pairings, operators and complex phases
entries.summary: Compare different color-space pairings while retaining exact complex amplitudes, and use the same R to transform two-body operators.

entries.title: 27 · From 4096 dimensions to multiplicity blocks: complete channels of four octets
entries.summary: Decompose 8⊗8⊗8⊗8 into 13 final types, distinguishing total space, isotypic subspaces, and path spaces of dimensions 8,32,33.

entries.title: 28 · Four-octet singlets: independently check 9j using δ invariants
entries.summary: Start with two normalized adjoint singlets and directly obtain the crossed-singlet amplitude 1/8 and probabilities aggregated by representation.

entries.title: 29 · exact high-dimensional complex states and adjoint two-body interactions
entries.summary: Retain all copies in the 32-path octet block and compare two-body operators for different pairings using exact  recoupling .

entries.title: 30 · 10,15,15′ and 27: identify the inputs before four-body recoupling
entries.summary: Place higher-dimensional representations on the four input leaves, and interpret exact results using Dynkin labels, conjugation, and independent permutation checks.

entries.title: 31 · Five paths with a 15 input: why do left and right copies look different?
entries.summary: For 15⊗3⊗3̄⊗3→24, count five paths in each tree and specify phases, copy bases, and quantities that can be compared.

entries.title: 32 · An exact four-body example with input 27: 42, weighted 9j, and complex amplitudes
entries.summary: Compute the five-path block of a final 42 within a 729-dimensional total space, checking results step by step with intermediate dimensions, Casimirs and complex phases.

entries.title: NaCl · sodium chloride: first identify the chemical basis
entries.summary: Different chemical species on the same geometric lattice cannot be exchanged arbitrarily. Use rocksalt to compare face-centering translations with pseudosymmetries exchanging Na and Cl.

entries.title: Si · Silicon: compensating translations and double-valued representations
entries.summary: Whether rotated atoms coincide depends on the translation part; electron spinors must also retain the minus sign left by a 360° turn.

entries.title: GaAs · gallium arsenide: similar geometry, different symmetry
entries.summary: Replace silicon’s two identical-element sublattices with Ga and As: inversion, which exchanged the two sets of basis atoms, no longer survives.

entries.title: Fe · iron: magnetization direction selects symmetries
entries.summary: For the same bcc nuclear structure, fixing magnetization retains only unitary or antiunitary combinations that preserve the moments.

entries.title: NiO · nickel oxide: antitranslation and the magnetic cell
entries.summary: Adjacent  ferromagnetic  planes along [111] alternate their moments. A chemical translation may break magnetic order, while  time reversal  combined with that translation restores it.

entries.title: MnF₂ · manganese difluoride: ligands determine antiferromagnetic symmetry
entries.summary: Looking only at two Mn atoms incorrectly suggests a half-translation symmetry. Including F ligands requires a combined rotation and translation to preserve the complete chemical structure.
